workflows-reference.purpose: Provide risk-tiered workflows for changing live infrastructure through declared state.

documentation-context.rule: Read docs/decisions/0001-orientation-lock.md first, including the recorded toolchain.
Read docs/architecture/infrastructure-layout.md before choosing where a change belongs.
Read docs/foundation/operations-principles.md before designing a change.
Read docs/process/change-workflow.md before planning a rollout.
Read relevant docs/modules notes and runbooks for the touched environment or component.

task-memory-gate.rule: Load Compass references/task-memory.xml when developer-approved gated design context must be preserved before implementation, even if the approved implementation has one slice.
Also load Compass references/task-memory.xml for long or risky work with at least two concrete implementation slices after alignment or design.
Implementation may not start until the task memory outcome is reported as created, resumed, or not-required.
When task memory is required, docs/.tasks/<task>/goal.md, diagram.md, and memories.md must exist before the first implementation edit or command.
Missing docs/_templates task memory files are a documentation gap, not permission to skip this gate.

risk-tiering.purpose: Every infra_change, hotfix_incident, and architecture_change slice gets exactly one tier. The tier decides approval, rehearsal, and rollback depth. This block is the source of truth for the tiers; the project may adapt them.

tier.name: no runtime effect
tier.covers: Lint, formatting, tags, comments, or defaults that do not change what runs.
tier.gate: Static validation and normal review. No live command is needed.

tier.name: reversible configuration
tier.covers: Configuration or variable contract changes with limited scope that revert cleanly.
tier.gate: Plan or dry-run evidence, explicit approval before apply, and live verification after apply.

tier.name: service-affecting
tier.covers: Changes that restart, reload, reconfigure, or scale a service, or change network or firewall rules, and can still be reverted.
tier.gate: Tier B gates, plus per-slice approval and a structured rollback plan with revert method, verification, and time estimate.

tier.name: destructive or hard to reverse
tier.covers: Data deletion, resource destroy or replace, reboot of stateful nodes, secret destruction, or changes that can lock operators out.
tier.gate: Tier C gates, plus double approval, a written runbook before apply, and backup or snapshot evidence.

risk-tiering.rule: Assign the tier during change-discovery and state it in the change record.
If a plan or dry-run shows a destroy or replace, the tier is at least C, whatever was assigned earlier.
There is no emergency tier. Incidents use hotfix_incident, and approval before each mutating command still applies.
When no environment exists to rehearse a Tier B or higher change, mark the slice not-staged and treat the first live run with extra care.

workflow.description: Change one live environment concern through declared state, with tiered gates.

enforcement.rule: Run phases sequentially: change-discovery, change-design, declared-state-implementation, live-rollout.
Execute one change slice per workflow; split unrelated environments or components into pending slices.
Before implementation starts, satisfy the task-memory-gate for any change with gated design context or long/risky multi-slice risk.
Apply the Compass Live Environment Gate to every command that mutates a live environment.

phase.name: change-discovery
phase.purpose: Know the current live state and the blast radius before deciding the change.

actions.action: Read the layout, principles, and change workflow docs.
Compare declared state with live state for the touched scope, and record drift as a finding before planning.
Name the environments, hosts, resources, and state in scope, and what depends on them.
Assign one risk tier and draft the rollback plan in the format for that tier.
State non-goals and the environments that must not change.

phase-output.scope: Environments, resources, and state in scope.
phase-output.live-state: Observed live state and drift findings.
phase-output.risk-tier: A, B, C, or D with reason.

phase.name: change-design
phase.purpose: Design the declared-state change and its verification before editing.

actions.action: Choose the files to change from docs/architecture/infrastructure-layout.md.
Define the apply order when the change spans several states or environments.
Define the verification matrix: static checks, plan or dry-run expectations, and live checks after apply.
List the secrets and credentials the change reads or writes.

phase-output.apply-order: Order across states or environments, or a single step.
phase-output.secrets-touched: Secrets read or written, or none.
phase-output.docs-impact: Docs, runbooks, or decisions to update.

phase.name: declared-state-implementation
phase.purpose: Change the declared state without touching live environments.

actions.action: Before the first implementation edit or command, report the task memory outcome: created, resumed, or not-required.
Edit only the declared state approved in change-design.
Run static validation for the toolchain: formatting, linting, syntax, and policy checks.
Stop and report before running any command that contacts a live environment.

phase.name: live-rollout
phase.purpose: Apply the change to live environments through the tier gates.

actions.action: Run the plan or dry-run for the exact change and show its summary, including destroy or replace counts.
Confirm or raise the risk tier from the plan, and restate the rollback plan.
Get approval for each mutating command as the tier requires, then apply in the approved order.
Verify the resulting live state against the verification matrix; re-reading command output is not verification.
Record what changed, the approvals, and the verification evidence, and update runbooks or docs when operations changed.

phase-output.approvals: Approvals given and for which commands.
phase-output.live-verification: Checks run against the live environment and their results.
phase-output.remaining-risk: Drift, follow-up, or cleanup still open.

workflow.evidence: Risk tier, rollback plan, static validation, plan or dry-run summary, approvals, and live verification.

workflow.description: Restore a live service quickly while keeping every mutation approved and recorded.

enforcement.rule: Phase order may be shortened, but approval before each mutating command still applies.
Break-glass console or CLI changes are recorded immediately: what, when, who, and why.
The incident is not closed until declared state matches live state again.

phase.name: stabilize
phase.purpose: Restore service with the smallest safe action.

actions.action: State the symptom, the affected environments, and the smallest safe action.
Show the dry-run or expected effect of the action when the tool supports it, and get approval before running it.
Verify from the live environment that the service is restored.

phase-output.action-taken: Commands run, approvals, and break-glass records.

phase.name: reconcile
phase.purpose: Bring declared state and live state back together.

actions.action: Compare live state with declared state and list every break-glass change.
Open an infra_change to write the fix into declared state, or to revert the live change.
Record the root cause and follow-up work.

phase-output.drift: Differences between live and declared state.
phase-output.follow-up: The infra_change and other follow-up work.

workflow.evidence: Symptom, approved actions, break-glass record, live verification, and the reconciling infra_change.

workflow.description: Change environment topology, state boundaries, or platform shape.

enforcement.rule: Record the decision in docs/decisions before implementation.
Assign a tier to each migration slice; moves across state boundaries are usually Tier C or D.
Run each migration slice through the infra_change phases.

phase.name: topology-design
phase.purpose: Agree on the target shape and a safe migration path.

actions.action: Describe the current and target topology, including state ownership.
Split the migration into slices with apply order and a rollback plan per slice.
Draft the decision record with options, rationale, and consequences.

phase-output.migration-slices: Ordered slices with tiers and rollback plans.

phase.name: migration-slices
phase.purpose: Execute one approved migration slice at a time.

actions.action: Run the current slice through the infra_change phases.
Stop after each verified slice and ask before continuing.

workflow.evidence: Decision record, slice plan, and per-slice infra_change evidence.

workflow.description: Evaluate tools, providers, or approaches without changing live environments.

enforcement.rule: Do not run commands that mutate a live environment.
Read-only inspection with production credentials needs developer approval first.

phase.name: investigate
phase.purpose: Answer one question with evidence and a recommendation.

actions.action: State the question and the constraints.
Compare at least two options with sources or measurements.
Recommend one option and name the follow-up change type.

workflow.evidence: Question, compared options, evidence, and recommendation.
